narrative:
Your loan application was denied because your estimated chance of default was 51 percent, just above the bank’s risk threshold. Although the margin was narrow, the assessment places you as a slightly worse risk than the bank accepts.

The strongest reason was your checking account. It is currently below zero, and only about 12.6 percent of approved applicants had a negative balance at application time. This suggests immediate money-management difficulties, and it influenced the decision more than any other factor.

Next in importance was your credit history: you have no credits or all previous credits were paid. This category is rare among approved applicants, appearing in only about 1 percent of cases. The lack of an established repayment record gives the bank less evidence that you will handle future payments reliably.

One thing helped: you own real estate. This was the third strongest factor and pointed toward lower risk. Property ownership signals stability and provides the bank a form of security. But it could not outweigh the checking account and credit history concerns.

To improve your chances, bring your checking account into positive territory and build a visible repayment history, perhaps with a small loan or credit card repaid consistently. Reapplying once those patterns are established would show stronger evidence that you are a safe borrower.
